model_reported.summary: Proposed a contrasting, conservative per-worker cutoff after comparing the two measured OpenMP variants; performance remains to be measured.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: Relied on existing evidence that the target build has validated OpenMP candidates; no new environment inspection or commands were performed.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The experiment reuses the same static OpenMP constructs as already measured candidates, so no unresolved API or compiler property required documentation research.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared only the supplied aggregate measurements and called out the lack of per-size overhead data; the controller must measure this proposal.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as evidence that the OpenMP outer loop can preserve varied-input correctness, not as proof that a particular cutoff is optimal or that every size benefits.
memory_lessons.claim: The two measured OpenMP variants were correct on eight varied cases and averaged 1.4078 ms and 1.4301 ms, respectively, versus the serial baseline mean of 7.5286 ms. These aggregate results do not isolate small-work overhead or the effect of their different cutoffs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a substantially coarser per-effective-worker cutoff and inspect available sizes and thread counts near the resulting serial/parallel boundary.

proposal.hypothesis: The two measured OpenMP variants use per-worker cutoffs of 512 and 256 options, with similar means and no per-size timings available. Requiring at least 1024 options per effective worker tests the contrasting assumption that a coarser grain avoids parallel overhead on medium workloads while retaining static-scheduled parallelism for large workloads. The controller should compare the resulting serial/parallel boundary against the baseline and earlier variants; no gain is assumed.

retained: Factored the unchanged Black-Scholes per-option formula into a helper shared by serial and parallel paths.
Added an OpenMP outer loop with static scheduling, requesting no more than min(threads,n) workers and avoiding nested teams.
Used a generic cutoff of 1024 options per effective worker to retain a serial path for small workloads and contrast earlier lower cutoffs.
